_comment: THE DENOMINATORS FOR THE pg_cron DEAD-MAN'S SWITCH.
public.pg_cron_watchdog_check() records how many cron.job rows it examined and how
many public.cron_job_manifest rows it judged them against. Both are equality-checked
against this file by scripts/check-cron-watchdog-checkin.mjs, because a fresh check-in
over a shrunken sweep is the most convincing false pass available: 'checked nothing'
and 'found nothing' produce the same green tick without a denominator.
A count that FELL means something disappeared. A count that ROSE means something was
added and this file was not raised to match — which is the correct moment to declare
it in public.cron_job_manifest too, or the watchdog will already be calling it an
unknown_job. Update BOTH, in the same change, or neither.
SELECT count(*) FROM cron.job;                   -> 24, +1 for cron-watchdog-every-15m = 25
SELECT count(*) FROM public.cron_job_manifest;   -> 27 (25 scheduled + 2 unscheduled_expected)
